covers.note: Curated in monthly batches. Days past the last date use scripts/live_lookup.py until the next batch is published.

rights.statement: The Library of Congress believes that the newspapers in Chronicling America are in the public domain or have no known copyright restrictions. Newspapers published in the United States more than 95 years ago are in the public domain in their entirety.

family_mode.preview_note: Old papers report crime and disasters like papers do today. I steer kids to the gentle parts, but please preview each page first: open the full page link before you share it.

family_levels.ok: Nothing a parent needs to explain in the big headlines or photos.
family_levels.care: A headline or item is about crime, death, disaster or scandal, told without gore, or the page uses a period term for a group of people in small print. Family mode stays on the spots and adds a parent note naming what to skip.
family_levels.no: Graphic violence, suicide, lynching, cannibalism, slurs, or disaster photos with bodies. Never shown in family mode.

standards.note: Supports practice toward these standards. Not a full curriculum and not accredited.

D2.His.2.3-5.text: Compare life in specific historical time periods to life today.

D2.His.2.6-8.text: Classify series of historical events and developments as examples of change and/or continuity.

D2.His.10.3-5.text: Compare information provided by different historical sources about the past.

D2.His.11.3-5.text: Infer the intended audience and purpose of a historical source from information within the source itself.

RI.3.7.text: Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

RH.6-8.7.text: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.
